questions.question:

What is the time period for 1 complete swing?

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 1 row: answer B

questions.question:
A student investigates the motion of a ball rolling down a slope.

The diagram shows the speed v of the ball at different times t.

Which statement describes the motion of the ball?

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 2 row: answer A

questions.question: Which statement about acceleration is correct?
options: It is related to the changing speed of an object.
It is the distance an object travels in one second.
It is the force acting on an object divided by the distance it travels in one second.
It is the force acting on an object when it is near to the Earth.

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 3 row: answer A

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the effects of placing a heavy load in a car?
options: It is easier to accelerate the car and easier to bring the car to rest.
It is easier to accelerate the car but more difficult to bring the car to rest.
It is more difficult to accelerate the car and more difficult to bring the car to rest.
It is more difficult to accelerate the car but easier to bring the car to rest.

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 4 row: answer C

questions.question:
A mass of 6.0 kg rests on the surface of a planet.

On this planet, g = 20 N / kg.

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 5 row: answer D

questions.question:
The mass of a measuring cylinder is 190 g.

400 cm³ of liquid is put into the measuring cylinder.

The total mass of the measuring cylinder and the liquid is 560 g.

Four solid objects are lowered in turn into the liquid. The densities of the objects are shown.

1 0.40 g / cm³
2 0.90 g / cm³
3 1.2 g / cm³
4 2.7 g / cm³

Which objects will float in the liquid?

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 6 row: answer B

questions.question:
The diagram shows a wooden beam PQ, of negligible weight, which is attached to a wall by a hinge at P and kept in a horizontal position by a vertical rope attached at Q.

The beam is 3.0 m in length.

A man of weight 800 N walks along the beam from P to Q.

What is the distance of the man from P when the tension in the rope at Q becomes equal to 500 N?

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 7 row: answer C

questions.question: Which quantity is a vector?

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 8 row: answer A

questions.question:

answer.evidence: mark scheme page 18, Question 9 row: answer A

questions.question:
The diagram shows part of a rollercoaster ride with the car at different positions.

questions.question:
A gas is heated in a sealed container.

The volume of the container does not change.

The average kinetic energy of the molecules increases.
The mass of each molecule increases.
The volume of each molecule increases.

questions.question: Why are metals better thermal conductors than other solids?
options: Metals contain free electrons which help transfer the energy.
Molecules in metals are in fixed positions.
Molecules in metals can move freely.
Molecules in metals vibrate faster than those in other solids.

questions.question:
Two freezers X and Y are identical except that one has a door opening at the front and the other has a door opening at the top.

questions.question:

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
options: The speed of light in glass is equal to the speed of light in a vacuum multiplied by the refractive index of glass.
The incident angle of a light ray at an air-glass surface is the angle between the ray and the glass surface.
The sine of the critical angle at an air-glass surface is equal to 1 / refractive index of glass.
The angle of refraction for light passing through an air-glass surface is proportional to the angle of incidence at that surface.

Sound travels through air as a series of compressions and rarefactions.

In a compression the wavelength is shorter than in a rarefaction.
In a compression the density of the air is greater than in a rarefaction.
In a compression the density of the air is lower than in a rarefaction.

questions.question:
Four nails A, B, C and D are tested to find which makes the strongest permanent magnet.

One of the nails is placed against a bar magnet and the number of paper clips which the nail can support is recorded.

questions.question:
The circuit shows one method of magnetising a steel bar.

How can the circuit be altered so that it can be used to demagnetise the magnetised steel bar?

replace the d.c. supply with an a.c. supply and gradually reduce the supply voltage to zero
reverse the polarity of the d.c. supply
